newsitem.title: LUXEMBOURG: Court looks at power supply customs tax classification.
newsitem.headline: Court looks at power supply customs tax classification.

text.p: The European Court of Justice said on Tuesday an electrical apparatus which is an uninterruptible power supply falls under the tariff subheading of transformers and static converters.

The court decided an uninterruptible power supply consisting of a cabinet containing a rectifier/charger, an inverter and a static bypass switch and another cabinet housing a sealed lead-acid accumulator battery falls under the customs tariff subheading 85.01B.II of transformers, static converters, rectifiers and rectifying apparatus.

The court looked at the "essential character" of the product in dispute before the Portuguese administrative court to determine its classification. Finding the product was designed to regulate and ensure a permanent power supply, the court found that the rectifier/charger cabinet gave it its essential character, and the accumulator cabinet was only of secondary importance.
Common Customs Tariff - Electrical apparatus constituting an uninterruptible power supply"
Reference to the court by the Supremo Tribunal Administrativo for a preliminary ruling pending before that court between
Codisel - Sociedade de Apoio Tecnico a Industria Ld
on the interpretation of Council regulation (EEC) No 950/68 on the Common Customs Tariff (OJ English Special Edition 1968(I), p. 275) as amended

Council regulation (EEC) No 950/68 on the Common Customs Tariff as amended, must be interpreted as meaning that an electrical apparatus which is an "uninterruptible power supply consisting, on the one hand, of a cabinet containing a rectifier/charger, an inverter and a static bypass switch and, on the other, of a cabinet housing a sealed lead-acid accumulator battery must be classifed under tariff subheading 85.01B.II of transformers, static converters, rectifiers and rectifying apparatus.
